library_preparation_preflight.summary: azure-identity is fully resolvable via a plain testImplementation dependency; no extra Maven coordinate or Docker image is needed, but tests should target specific credential types with a mocked local HTTP endpoint rather than DefaultAzureCredential to stay hermetic and fast.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Prefer instantiating specific credential classes directly (ClientSecretCredential, ClientCertificateCredential, UsernamePasswordCredential, ManagedIdentityCredential, EnvironmentCredential) over DefaultAzureCredential: the default chain probes the IMDS endpoint and shells out to az/pwsh/azd via ProcessBuilder, which is slow/flaky without network access or those CLIs installed. To exercise the MSAL4J/Jackson/JWT reflection paths meaningfully, set a custom httpClient(...) on the credential builder backed by a local com.sun.net.httpserver mock that returns a fake AAD token JSON response (same pattern already used in tests/src/com.azure/azure-core-http-jdk-httpclient), or simply assert on the expected authentication failure when using fake tenant/client/secret values. No AZURE_* environment variables are required unless a test specifically wants to exercise EnvironmentCredential's own code path.
risks: If the generated scaffold defaults to DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder().build().getToken(...), the credential chain's IMDS probe and CLI subprocess attempts (az/pwsh/azd) may cause slow or flaky test/native-image runs in a sandboxed environment with no network egress or those tools installed.

msal4j and azure-core-http-netty are new transitive surfaces for this repo (no existing metadata) and native-image builds may need iterative --initialize-at-build-time fixes similar to those already applied for azure-core-http-jdk-httpclient; this should be handled by the normal generate/fix workflow rather than pre-declared here.
